mainTopic: The laws of ראשית הגז, and the גמרא's search for why consecrated and jointly owned sheep are exempt.
overview: This amud opens the perek on ראשית הגז, the first wool that goes to a כהן. The משנה says the מצוה applies everywhere and at all times, but only to חולין and only to sheep. There must also be 'many' sheep: two according to בית שמאי and five according to בית הלל. It then sets the size of the gift and rules that dyed wool is exempt while washed wool is not. It also explains who gives when fleece is bought from a גוי or from a fellow Jew. The גמרא asks why קדשים are exempt and works through several cases built on the word 'צאנך': animals consecrated for בדק הבית, an animal consecrated except for its wool and its weakening, and why altar animals cannot fit these cases, since their holiness spreads through the whole animal. רבא instead learns the exemption from 'גז צאנך תתן לו', which teaches that nothing may come between shearing and giving. That frees the word צאנך. For רבי אלעאי it exempts partners, and for the רבנן it exempts a partnership with a גוי. The amud ends with their dispute over whether the two halves of the פסוק can be learned from each other.

steps.title: Where and when the first-shearing gift applies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that ראשית הגז applies in and outside ארץ ישראל, with or without the בית המקדש, and only to חולין, not קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of giving the first wool to the כהן applies in Israel and outside Israel, whether or not the Temple is standing. It applies to ordinary animals, not to animals dedicated to the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the new topic by giving the basic range of the מצוה of ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This מצוה is not tied to the Land or to the בית המקדש. So it applies everywhere and at all times. The one limit is that it applies to ordinary (חולין) animals, not to consecrated (מוקדשים) ones.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing: a portion of the first wool shorn, given to a כהן
Outside ארץ ישראל
While the בית המקדש is standing
Ordinary, non-sacred animals
Animals consecrated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: The first shearing applies
phrases.notes: This is the first wool the owner gives to a כהן (דברים 18:4).

phrases.english: in the Land and outside the Land,
when the Temple stands and when the Temple does not stand,
with non-sacred animals, but not with consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek on ראשית הגז.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז applies everywhere and at all times, but only to חולין.

steps.title: Why the foreleg, jaw and maw gift is stricter than the first shearing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares the two gifts. זרוע, לחיים וקבה apply to cattle and sheep and to any number of animals. ראשית הגז applies only to sheep, and only when there are many.
steps.simpleTranslation: The gift of the foreleg, jaw and maw is stricter than the first shearing. It applies to cattle and to sheep, and to many animals or few. The first shearing applies only to sheep, and only when there are many.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares ראשית הגז with another gift to the כהן, זרוע, לחיים וקבה, and shows that the other gift has a wider reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison has two points. Point one is the type of animal: cattle and sheep, versus sheep only. Point two is the number of animals: any amount, versus only 'many.' The second point raises the obvious question of what counts as 'many,' which the משנה asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency: a way one law is stricter than another
The foreleg, jaw and maw, given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal
Cattle
Sheep (as opposed to goats)
A small number

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'stricter' here only means it applies in more cases. It does not mean ראשית הגז is a lesser מצוה when it does apply.

phrases.english: There is a stringency in the foreleg, the jaw and the maw
phrases.notes: These are parts of a slaughtered animal given to a כהן (דברים 18:3).

phrases.english: compared to the first shearing:
that the foreleg, the jaw and the maw
apply to cattle and to sheep,
to many animals and to few,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּרְחֵלוֹת,
phrases.english: but the first shearing applies only to sheep,
and applies only to many animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּזְּרוֹעַ וּלְחָיַיִם וּבַקֵּבָה מֵרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further limits on ראשית הגז by comparing it to another gift to the כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז applies only to sheep, and only to a large number. זרוע, לחיים וקבה apply to cattle and sheep in any number.

steps.title: How many sheep count as 'many'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how many sheep are needed to count as 'many.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many is 'many'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The משנה is getting ready to explain the word 'many' that it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said ראשית הגז needs 'many' sheep but gave no number. This question opens the מחלוקת that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: How many / how much
A large number: here, the minimum flock size for ראשית הגז

phrases.english: And how many is "many"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of 'many' from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of sheep that creates the obligation of ראשית הגז.

steps.title: Two sheep or five: the dispute and its verses
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say two sheep, based on ישעיהו. בית הלל say five, based on שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say two sheep, because a verse says 'a man shall keep alive a young cow and two sheep.' בית הלל say five, because a verse says 'five sheep prepared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question with a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. Each side proves its number from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls the flock 'צאנך,' your flock. Each side looks for the smallest group that a פסוק calls צאן. בית שמאי find a פסוק that calls two animals צאן. בית הלל find one that calls five animals צאן.

keyTerms.meaning: He will keep alive / raise
Two sheep: a pair called צאן
Five prepared sheep: five called צאן

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two sheep,
as it is said: "A man shall keep alive a young cow
and two sheep,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 7:21. Two animals are called צאן, the same word the תורה uses for this מצוה.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: five,
as it is said: "Five sheep prepared."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 25:18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי say two sheep and בית הלל say five, each based on a פסוק that calls that number צאן.

steps.title: Does each sheep need to give a minimum amount of wool?
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says each of the five sheep must give a מנה and a half of wool. חכמים say five sheep giving any amount are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says: five sheep that each give a hundred and fifty dinars' weight of wool are obligated in the first shearing. חכמים say: five sheep giving any amount of wool are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: Working with בית הלל's number of five, the משנה brings a new מחלוקת: must each sheep give a minimum weight of wool?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא adds a requirement about the wool, not just the head count: each sheep must give a מנה and a half. חכמים say only the number of sheep matters, so any amount of wool counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Being shorn / yielding a shearing
A weight of one hundred dinars
Half (here, half a מנה)
Any amount at all

steps.whatToRemember: ראשית הגז applies only to sheep and needs 'many.' בית שמאי say two and בית הלל say five. On the amount of wool, רבי דוסא requires a מנה and a half per sheep, while חכמים say any amount.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
five sheep that are shorn
a maneh and a half each
phrases.notes: A מנה is a hundred dinars in weight, and פרס is half of that. So each sheep gives 150 dinars' weight.

phrases.english: are obligated in the first shearing,
and the Sages say:
five sheep that are shorn of any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the number five and adds a dispute about the amount of wool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: five sheep each giving a מנה and a half. חכמים: five sheep giving any amount.

steps.title: How much wool goes to the כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what amount of wool must be given to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much do we give him?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks how much wool the owner must hand over to the כהן. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 to 5 set the minimum number of sheep and amount of wool needed to create the obligation. Now the משנה asks a different question: once the obligation exists, how much does the כהן actually receive?

keyTerms.meaning: we give, meaning the owner gives to the כהן

phrases.english: And how much do we give him?
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן who receives ראשית הגז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount that creates the obligation to the amount that is given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the gift of ראשית הגז.

steps.title: Five Judean סלעים of clean wool, enough for a small garment
steps.stepSummary: The gift is the weight of five סלעים in יהודה, which equals ten in the גליל. It is measured as clean wool and must be enough to make a small garment, because the פסוק says 'you shall give him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The weight of five סלעים by the measure of יהודה, which is ten סלעים by the measure of the גליל. It is measured as cleaned wool, not dirty wool. It must be enough to make a small garment from it, as the פסוק says 'you shall give him,' meaning it must be big enough to count as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers that the כהן gets five Judean סלעים by weight of clean wool. That is enough to make a small garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three details are given. The weight is five Judean סלעים, and the Galilean סלע is half as heavy, so that equals ten Galilean סלעים. The wool is weighed as if it were clean, so the dirt doesn't count toward the amount. The reason for the amount comes from the words 'תתן לו': a gift has to be something useful, like enough wool for a small garment.

keyTerms.meaning: סלעים, a unit of weight (and coin)
cleaned or laundered
dirty, as wool is when it comes off the sheep
enough to count as a real gift

steps.confusionAlert: Five סלעים in יהודה and ten in the גליל are the same amount of wool. Only the size of the local סלע is different.

phrases.english: The weight of five sela in Judea,
which are ten sela in the Galilee,
phrases.notes: The Galilean סלע weighs half as much, so it takes ten of them.

phrases.english: laundered and not dirty,
phrases.notes: He means the amount is weighed as clean wool, so dirt in the fleece doesn't count.

phrases.english: enough to make a small garment from it,
as it is stated: "You shall give him,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: that it should contain enough for a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five Judean סלעים of clean wool, enough for a small garment, derived from 'תתן לו'.

steps.title: Dyeing the wool ends the obligation, laundering does not
steps.stepSummary: If the owner dyed the wool before giving it, he is exempt. If he only laundered it, he still must give.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not manage to give it to the כהן before he dyed it, he is exempt. If he laundered it but did not dye it, he is still obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on what happens if the owner changed the wool before giving it. Dyeing frees him from the obligation, but washing does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dyeing is a real change to the wool, so it counts as new and is no longer the 'first shearing' that must be given. Washing only cleans the wool, so it is still the same wool and the obligation stays.

keyTerms.meaning: he dyed it
he laundered or whitened it
exempt
obligated

phrases.english: If he did not manage to give it to him
until he dyed it, he is exempt;
if he laundered it but did not dye it, he is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לִיתְּנוֹ לוֹ עַד שֶׁצְּבָעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the amount, the משנה discusses when the obligation is lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dyed wool is exempt from ראשית הגז. Laundered wool is still obligated.

steps.title: Buying a גוי's fleece is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Someone who buys the fleece of a גוי's sheep while it is still attached, and shears it himself, does not give ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who buys the fleece of a גוי's sheep is exempt from ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins the laws of buying fleece. It rules first that wool bought from a גוי is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the fleece of your flock', so what matters is who owns the sheep at the shearing, not who owns the wool (Rashi). Buying only the attached fleece does not make the sheep his. The sheep still belong to the גוי, so the buyer has nothing to give.

keyTerms.meaning: the buyer
fleece, here bought while still attached to the sheep

phrases.english: One who purchases the fleece of the sheep of a gentile
is exempt from the first sheared wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: buying fleece.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי's fleece bought by a Jew is exempt.

steps.title: Buying a fellow Jew's fleece: who gives?
steps.stepSummary: If a Jewish seller kept some of the wool, the seller gives. If he sold all of it, the buyer gives.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who buys the fleece of another Jew's sheep: if the seller kept some, the seller is obligated. If he did not keep any, the buyer is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on buying wool from a fellow Jew. The answer depends on whether the seller kept any wool for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the obligation does exist, because the sheep belonged to a Jew. The only question is who pays it. If the seller still has wool, he gives from that. If he sold everything, the obligation goes with the wool to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: he kept back some for himself
the seller

phrases.english: One who purchases the fleece of the sheep of another,
phrases.notes: "Another" here means a fellow Jew, in contrast to the גוי in the line before.

phrases.english: if he kept some, the seller is obligated;
if he did not keep any, the buyer is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 9: buying from a Jew instead of a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seller kept some, the seller gives. If not, the buyer gives.

steps.title: Selling one type of fleece: each side gives for his own
steps.stepSummary: If the seller had two clearly different kinds of sheep and sold the fleece of only one kind, each person gives ראשית הגז from his own wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had two kinds of sheep, gray and white, and sold him the gray but not the white, or the males but not the females, then this one gives for himself and that one gives for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where the seller sold the fleece of one clear group of sheep. Here both seller and buyer give, each from his own wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, a seller who kept some wool covers the whole obligation. Here the wool split into two separate groups, like gray and white or male and female. Each group is treated as its own shearing, so each owner gives for his part.

keyTerms.meaning: gray or dark-colored sheep
white sheep
for himself, from his own share

steps.whatToRemember: With bought fleece: from a גוי, nobody gives. From a Jew who kept some, the seller gives. From a Jew who kept none, the buyer gives. If one distinct group was sold, each gives for his own.

phrases.english: If he had two types,
gray and white,

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ שְׁחוּפוֹת אֲבָל לֹא לְבָנוֹת,
phrases.english: and sold him the gray but not the white,
or the males but not the females,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹתֵן לְעַצְמוֹ וְזֶה נוֹתֵן לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: this one gives for himself and that one gives for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits Step 10: when the sale is of a distinct group, the seller's leftover wool does not cover the buyer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When distinct groups are sold, both seller and buyer give from their own wool.

steps.title: Why are sanctified animals exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason that ראשית הגז does not apply to קדשים, as Step 1 stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: With sanctified animals, what is the reason it does not apply?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source behind the משנה's rule that קדשים are exempt from ראשית הגז. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the מצוה applies only to חולין and not to קדשים, but gave no reason. The גמרא wants to know where that exemption comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
sanctified animals, set aside for the בית המקדש
what is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With sacrificial animals, what is the reason it does not apply?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first rule of the משנה to find its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוק for exempting קדשים from ראשית הגז.

steps.title: "Your flock" excludes sanctified animals
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'צאנך,' your flock. Sanctified animals belong to the הקדש, not to you, so they are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'your flock,' and not a flock of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the word 'צאנך' in the פסוק. Only sheep that belong to you are included, and הקדש animals do not belong to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'your' limits the מצוה to sheep that a person privately owns. Once an animal is sanctified, it belongs to the הקדש. Its wool therefore falls outside the מצוה of ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: your flock
consecrated property belonging to the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: קדשים are exempt from ראשית הגז because the פסוק says 'צאנך,' and sanctified animals are not 'yours.'

phrases.english: The verse states: "Your flock,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: and not a consecrated flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'צאנך' limits the מצוה to privately owned sheep, which excludes הקדש.

steps.title: Why would sanctified animals need a פסוק at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation from 'צאנך': קדשים cannot be sheared anyway, so the exemption should not need a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason we exempt them is because the Torah wrote 'your flock'? That implies that without it we would have said קדשים are obligated in ראשית הגז. But they cannot be sheared at all, as it says 'and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 13. If sanctified animals may never be sheared, why would we need the word 'צאנך' to exempt them from ראשית הגז?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 used 'צאנך' to exempt קדשים. But the Torah already forbids shearing a בכור, a sanctified animal. If there is no legal shearing, there is no ראשית הגז to give, so the פסוק seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have thought
Fit to be sheared
A firstborn animal, which is holy

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that קדשים are exempt. It is asking why a פסוק is needed when the exemption seems obvious.

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote "your flock"
which implies that if not for this, I would have said
sanctified animals are obligated in the first shearing?
But they are not fit for shearing,
as it is written: "And you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock"!
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

steps.triggerLanguage: טעמא דכתב רחמנא צאנך, הא לאו הכי הוה אמינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the derivation given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for 'צאנך' to exempt קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sanctified animals cannot be sheared at all, so no ראשית הגז could arise. The פסוק would be teaching nothing.

steps.title: The פסוק is about animals sanctified for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: For קדשי מזבח the challenge is correct. The פסוק comes for קדשי בדק הבית, which may be sheared.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were talking about animals sanctified for the altar, you would be right. Here we are dealing with animals sanctified for the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the exemption from 'צאנך' is not about altar animals. It is about animals donated to the בית המקדש's maintenance fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי מזבח cannot be sheared, so for them no פסוק is needed. קדשי בדק הבית are only valued for their money and have no Torah ban on shearing. So 'צאנך' is needed to exempt them.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals sanctified to be offered on the altar
Property sanctified for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Indeed so; you are right
Here, what case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: If it were about animals sanctified for the altar, indeed so.
Here, what are we dealing with?
With animals sanctified for the upkeep of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems pointless because all קדשים are forbidden to shear
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק exempts קדשי בדק הבית, which the Torah allows to be sheared

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says Temple-upkeep animals may not be sheared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי אלעזר: even קדשי בדק הבית are forbidden in shearing and work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say that animals sanctified for Temple upkeep are forbidden to be sheared or worked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 15 with a statement of רבי אלעזר. If these animals also may not be sheared, the original problem returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 relied on קדשי בדק הבית being allowed to be sheared. רבי אלעזר says they too are forbidden in shearing. So again there would be no shearing to obligate, and 'צאנך' would teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing
Using the animal for work
Forbidden

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Animals sanctified for the upkeep of the Temple
are forbidden in shearing and in work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קדשי בדק הבית may be sheared
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אלעזר forbids shearing them, they are just like altar animals, and the פסוק is again unnecessary.

steps.title: The ban is only rabbinic, so a sheared animal might have owed the gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's ban is מדרבנן. By Torah law they may be sheared, so one might have thought that a person who sheared them must give ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ban is only rabbinic. You might have thought: since by Torah law they may be sheared, if someone did shear it, he should give the first shearing to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's ban is only from the חכמים. On the Torah level shearing is allowed, so the פסוק is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic ban does not change the Torah status of the animal. If someone broke the rabbinic rule and sheared, we might think a Torah obligation of ראשית הגז kicks in. 'צאנך' teaches that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: From the rabbis, not from the Torah
From Torah law
It would enter your mind to say
He should give it to him (the כהן)

phrases.english: That is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר's ban on shearing comes from the חכמים, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
since by Torah law they are fit for shearing,
where he did shear it,
he should give it to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כהן who receives ראשית הגז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing a rabbinic ban from Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אלעזר forbids shearing, the פסוק is unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is only rabbinic. On the Torah level shearing is allowed, so the פסוק is needed to exempt sheared wool

steps.title: But the wool itself is sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the wool belongs to הקדש, so it obviously cannot be given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he sanctified it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 17. Even if he sheared, the wool is holy property, so how could anyone think to give it to a כהן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animal was dedicated to the בית המקדש, its wool is also הקדש. A person cannot give away הקדש as a gift. So again it seems obvious that no ראשית הגז is owed, without any פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He sanctified, made it holy property
Property belonging to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But he sanctified it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one might have given ראשית הגז from sheared בדק הבית wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wool is הקדש and cannot be given to a כהן, so the פסוק is again unnecessary.

steps.title: One might have required redeeming the wool and then giving it
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought the owner must redeem the wool from הקדש and then give ראשית הגז. The פסוק teaches he need not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: he should redeem it and then give it to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is still needed. Without it, we might have required the owner to buy the wool back from הקדש and then give the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקדש can be redeemed by paying its value to the Temple treasury. After that it is ordinary wool that could go to a כהן. 'צאנך' teaches that there is no such obligation, because the wool was never 'your flock'.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem, buying back holy property for its value
Redemption of הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: So far: 'צאנך' exempts קדשי בדק הבית from ראשית הגז. Their shearing is forbidden only מדרבנן, and without the פסוק we might have required redeeming the wool and giving it to the כהן. The next steps challenge this explanation from the rule of העמדה והערכה.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
he should redeem it and give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: סלקא דעתך אמינא לפרוק וליתיב ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 and secures the derivation of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a real possibility the פסוק comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the wool is הקדש, it obviously cannot be given, so the פסוק is unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the פסוק we would require redeeming the wool and then giving it. 'צאנך' removes that obligation

steps.title: Redeeming needs standing and valuation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the last answer. Redeeming from הקדש requires העמדה והערכה, and that cannot be done to sheared wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But redeeming requires standing the item before the כהן and having him value it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 19, which said one might have thought the owner must redeem the wool and then give ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redemption of a הקדש animal needs העמדה והערכה: it is stood before the כהן, who sets its value. Wool that has been cut off cannot go through this, so it could never be redeemed. That means there was never a reason to think he must redeem it, and the פסוק would not be needed to teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal before the כהן
The כהן setting a value on it
But it requires...

phrases.english: But it requires standing and valuation!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11–12. Wool that has been cut off can't be stood before the כהן, so it couldn't be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הוה אמינא offered in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one might have thought the owner must redeem the wool from הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sheared wool cannot undergo העמדה והערכה, so it cannot be redeemed. The supposed הוה אמינא never existed.

steps.title: The problem remains for one view
steps.stepSummary: The objection works only if בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה. For the view that they do not, there is no problem. For the view that they do, a new answer is needed, which step 22 gives.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to the one who said that קדשי בדק הבית were not included in standing and valuation. But according to the one who said they were included, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. Step 19's answer survives for one opinion, but for the other opinion we still need a new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת whether קדשי בדק הבית need העמדה והערכה at all. If they do not, the wool could be redeemed without it, and step 19 is fine. If they do, the wool cannot be redeemed, and the הוה אמינא falls apart. The גמרא now needs a new explanation of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view)
What can be said? (the question remains)
Included in

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who said
animals consecrated for Temple maintenance
were not included in standing and valuation,
but according to the one who said they were included,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the objection of step 20 to one opinion and keeps it alive for that opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 19's explanation of the פסוק, according to the view that בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For that view, wool can never be redeemed, so the פסוק cannot be teaching that one need not redeem it.

steps.title: He consecrated the animal but kept the wool
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש, in the name of רבי ינאי, explains that the case is an animal given to בדק הבית except for its wool. The wool belongs to the owner, yet צאנך exempts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: Here we are dealing with someone who consecrated his animal for בדק הבית except for its fleece. You might have thought: let him shear it and give ראשית הגז. So the verse says 'your flock', and not a flock of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer explains what the פסוק is teaching. The owner kept the wool for himself, so we might have thought he owes ראשית הגז on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the wool was never הקדש, no redemption is needed, and the problem of העמדה והערכה disappears. The wool really is his, so there was a real reason to think he must give ראשית הגז. The פסוק צאנך teaches that the animal itself must be his ordinary flock, not a הקדש animal.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates (makes something הקדש)
Except for its fleece
It might enter your mind to say
Your flock
Sheep that belong to הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The wool here is NOT הקדש. It belongs to the owner. The exemption comes because the animal itself is הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the פסוק a real job without needing redemption, so it works even for the view that requires העמדה והערכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי בַּר פַּטִּישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Pattish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
Here it is about one who consecrates his animal for Temple maintenance
except for its fleece.
It might enter your mind to say:
let him shear and give it [to the כהן],
the verse says: 'Your flock',
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: and not a flock of consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי בַּר פַּטִּישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי הָכָא בְּמַקְדִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question of step 21 by setting up a new case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so redemption is not needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the wool belongs to the owner, he must shear it and give ראשית הגז
steps.terutzMaskana: צאנך excludes an animal that is הקדש, even when the wool was kept back

steps.title: Why not altar animals too?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is an animal consecrated except for its wool, why limit it to בדק הבית? It could also be קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then קדשי מזבח too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. Why say the פסוק comes only for בדק הבית animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 15) the גמרא said the פסוק cannot be about קדשי מזבח, since they may not be sheared. But if the owner kept the wool, he could shear an altar animal too. So the פסוק could be talking about קדשי מזבח as well.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Animals consecrated for the altar

phrases.english: If so, animals consecrated for the altar too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the case to קדשי בדק הבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Keeping the wool back would work just as well for an altar animal, so why exclude קדשי מזבח?

steps.title: Shearing weakens the animal
steps.stepSummary: An altar animal still may not be sheared, because shearing weakens it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They become weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even if the wool is not הקדש, shearing an altar animal weakens it, so it stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal itself is still הקדש. Shearing makes it weaker, which harms holy property. So shearing a קדשי מזבח animal is still not allowed, and the case cannot be about them.

keyTerms.meaning: They become weakened

phrases.english: They become weakened.
phrases.notes: Shearing makes the animal weaker, and that hurts the holy animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a separate reason shearing is forbidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Keeping the wool lets one shear an altar animal
steps.terutzMaskana: Shearing weakens the הקדש animal, so it remains forbidden

steps.title: בדק הבית animals also get weakened
steps.stepSummary: The same weakness problem should apply to בדק הבית animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: קדשי בדק הבית also become weakened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against its own case. A בדק הבית animal is also weakened by shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If weakening forbids shearing an altar animal, it should also forbid shearing a בדק הבית animal. Then the case in step 22 would not work either.

keyTerms.meaning: Also

phrases.english: Animals consecrated for Temple maintenance also become weakened!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 24 to attack the case of step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a בדק הבית animal consecrated except for its wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weakening problem applies just as much to בדק הבית animals, so they should not be sheared either.

steps.title: He kept both the wool and the weakening
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the owner consecrated the animal to בדק הבית except for its wool and except for the weakening shearing causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he said: except for the shearing and the weakening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the case. The owner held back both the wool and the loss of strength from shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the weakening was never given to הקדש, shearing does not harm holy property. This works for בדק הבית, whose value is money. It does not work for an altar animal, so the פסוק צאנך is about this בדק הבית case.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing / fleece
Weakening, the loss of strength

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק צאנך exempts from ראשית הגז a בדק הבית animal whose owner kept its wool and its weakening for himself. Even though the wool is his, the animal is not 'your flock'.

phrases.english: Where he said: except for the shearing and the weakening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by refining the case of step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shearing a בדק הבית animal weakens it and is therefore forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner held back the weakening too, so shearing is allowed, and צאנך exempts it from ראשית הגז

steps.title: Why not an altar animal with the same two exceptions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the case must be limited to בדק הבית. An owner could consecrate an altar animal and also hold back the wool and the weakening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case could also be about קדשי מזבח, where the owner said: 'except for the shearing and the weakening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If holding back the weakening solves the problem for בדק הבית, why not use an altar animal the same way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said the owner held back both the wool and the weakening that shearing causes. That fix looks like it should work for קדשי מזבח too. So the limit to בדק הבית seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals consecrated for the altar, to be brought as offerings
Weakening; the loss of strength an animal suffers from being sheared
Except for; a condition that holds something back from the consecration

phrases.english: Animals consecrated for the altar too!
phrases.notes: In other words, why not say the case is about an altar animal as well?

phrases.english: Where he said: except for the shearing and the weakening,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the fix from step 26 to altar animals and asks why the case is limited to בדק הבית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limit of the case to בדק הבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If holding back the wool and the weakening works for בדק הבית, it should work equally for קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: With altar animals, holiness spreads through everything
steps.stepSummary: The condition doesn't work for altar animals. Their holiness spreads through the whole animal no matter what the owner says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the holiness spreads through all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner's condition fails for קדשי מזבח. The holiness takes over the entire animal anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בדק הבית, the owner can hold back the wool and the weakening. With an altar animal, קדושה spreads to the whole body, including the wool. So shearing it would still be forbidden, and the case can only work for בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness spreads out to cover the whole animal
Even so; despite what was just said

phrases.english: Even so,
the holiness spreads through all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between kinds of הקדש: the owner's condition works for בדק הבית but not for קדשי מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An owner can hold back wool and weakening from an altar animal just as from a בדק הבית animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Altar holiness spreads through the whole animal, so the condition fails and shearing stays forbidden.

steps.title: Where do we know holiness spreads?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that altar holiness spreads through the entire animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants a source for the rule it just used, and the next step brings one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 depends completely on the idea that altar holiness spreads. The גמרא will not accept that idea without proof, so it asks for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you say this? A request for a source

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule used in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that holiness from an altar consecration spreads through the whole animal.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: consecrating a leg makes the whole animal an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The source is רבי יוסי. Someone who says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה' has made the whole animal an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי said: Isn't it so with consecrated animals that one who says 'the leg of this animal is a burnt offering' makes the whole animal a burnt offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי יוסי. Consecrating just one part of an altar animal makes the whole animal holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If consecrating only a leg spreads to the whole body, then holding back the wool can't stop the spreading either. That is exactly the rule step 28 needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals, here meaning altar offerings
A burnt offering, burned entirely on the altar
Isn't it so that...? Introduces a well-known rule

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei said:
Isn't it so with consecrated animals
that one who says 'The leg of this one is a burnt offering'
– all of it is a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי rules that consecrating one limb as an עולה makes the whole animal an עולה, so altar holiness spreads.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר agrees when life depends on the part
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יוסי, but only about a part the animal can live without. If the consecrated part is something its life depends on, everyone agrees the whole animal is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי מאיר, who says it is not entirely an עולה, that applies only when he consecrated something the animal's life does not depend on. But if he consecrated something its life depends on, it is consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off an objection: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יוסי. It shows that even רבי מאיר agrees in our kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says holiness doesn't spread from a leg, because an animal can live without its leg. When the consecrated part is something the animal's life depends on, even he agrees the whole animal becomes holy. Here the owner consecrated the animal's body itself, so the holiness spreads according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only; limits a rule to a specific case
A body part the animal's life depends on

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not reject the idea of spreading altogether. He only says it doesn't happen from a part the animal can live without.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir
who said it is not entirely a burnt offering,
that applies only where he consecrated
something the animal's life does not depend on,
but if he consecrated something
that its life depends on – it is consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר אֵין כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the proof of step 30 by showing that even the opposing view agrees in this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the disagreement to cases where the animal can live without the consecrated part.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof only works according to רבי יוסי, since רבי מאיר disagrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the consecrated part is something the animal's life depends on, everyone agrees the whole animal becomes holy.

steps.title: רבא: the owner consecrated only the wool
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different explanation. The case is someone who consecrated the fleece itself. We might have thought he should shear it, redeem it, and give it to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is one who consecrates the fleece itself. You might have thought: let him shear it, redeem it, and give it to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the whole 'animal except for the wool' approach and offers a simpler case. Then he sets up a reasoning that the next step will reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case the sheep itself is not holy at all; only its wool belongs to הקדש. So we might think the owner could shear it, redeem the wool, and still give it as ראשית הגז. The verse in the next step will rule this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Fleece; the wool sheared from the sheep
It might enter your mind to say; introduces a mistaken first thought
Let him redeem; buy back from הקדש by paying its value

phrases.english: Rava said:
The case is one who consecrates the fleece itself,
it might enter your mind to say:
let him shear, redeem, and give it to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of רבי מני בר פטיש (steps 22–31) with a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wool consecrated by itself could be sheared, redeemed, and then given to the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Set up here; it is resolved by the verse in the next step.

steps.title: Nothing may come between shearing and giving
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'גז צאנך תתן לו' teaches that ראשית הגז applies only when all that is missing is shearing and giving. Consecrated wool also needs פדיה, so it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The sheared wool of your flock you shall give him.' This means wool that is missing only shearing and giving. That excludes this wool, which is missing shearing, redemption, and giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse to reject the mistaken thought from step 32. It concludes רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse places shearing right next to giving. So the obligation applies only when nothing else stands in between. Consecrated wool needs an extra step, פדיה, so it falls outside ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking; still needing a certain action
Redemption; buying something back from הקדש
Giving; handing the wool to the כהן

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, ראשית הגז applies only to wool that needs nothing more than shearing and giving. Wool that would also need פדיה is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, simpler way to explain why consecrated wool is exempt from ראשית הגז, based on the order of actions in the verse.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'The sheared wool of your flock you shall give him,'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: meaning wool that is not lacking
anything except shearing and giving,
which excludes this, which is lacking
shearing, redemption, and giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken thought of step 32 using the verse.
steps.raayaObject: Consecrated wool is exempt from ראשית הגז even after it is redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 18:4, 'גז צאנך תתן לו', read as requiring nothing between shearing and giving.

steps.title: What does the word 'your flock' come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: If the exemption of הקדש comes from 'גז … תתן', what is the extra word צאנך there for?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the word 'your flock' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what job the word צאנך has, now that the exemption of consecrated wool comes from a different part of the פסוק. This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא will find a use for the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone could have said צאנך ('your own flock, not הקדש') is what exempts consecrated sheep. רבא learned that exemption from 'גז … תתן' instead. So the word צאנך now looks extra, and the גמרא needs to find what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: For what does it come? What is this word teaching?
'Your flock.' The word in the פסוק about ראשית הגז

phrases.english: But for what does 'your flock' come?
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4. Since step 33 learned the הקדש exemption from 'גז … תתן', the word צאנך needs its own job.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's derivation by asking what the remaining word in the פסוק teaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word צאנך excludes, now that it is not needed for הקדש.

steps.title: Partners' sheep: the רבנן obligate and רבי אלעאי exempts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says partners' sheep are obligated in ראשית הגז, but רבי אלעאי exempts them, learning from צאנך ('yours') that partnership is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: an animal owned by partners is obligated in ראשית הגז, and רבי אלעאי exempts it. What is רבי אלעאי's reason? The פסוק says 'your flock,' and not one owned in partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that צאנך is needed for a ברייתא. According to רבי אלעאי, the word excludes sheep owned by partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your' is in the singular, so רבי אלעאי reads it as a flock that belongs to one person, not to partners. The רבנן disagree and obligate partners. This gives צאנך a clear use for רבי אלעאי. The next step explains what it teaches the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal owned jointly by partners
Exempts
Partnership, joint ownership

phrases.english: For that which is taught: an animal of partners
is obligated in the first shearing,
and Rabbi Ilai exempts.
What is the reason of Rabbi Ilai?
The verse says 'your flock,'
and not one of partnership.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא: בֶּהֱמַת הַשּׁוּתָּפִים חַיָּיב בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 34 by giving צאנך a job: excluding partners, according to רבי אלעאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אלעאי, צאנך excludes sheep owned in partnership.
steps.confusionAlert: The partnership here is between two Jews. A partnership with a גוי comes up separately in the next steps.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'your flock' to exclude a partnership with a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן, who obligate partners, use צאנך to exempt sheep owned together with a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They use it to exclude a partnership with a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks briefly what צאנך teaches the רבנן, and answers in the same breath: it exempts a flock shared with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן obligate two Jewish partners, so for them צאנך cannot exclude partnership in general. They read it more narrowly: 'your' means owned by Jews, so a flock shared with a non-Jew is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; the word limits the law
A partnership with a non-Jew

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: A short question: if the רבנן obligate partners, what does 'your flock' teach them?

phrases.english: To exclude partnership with a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the meaning of צאנך according to the other side of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן, צאנך exempts a flock co-owned with a גוי.

steps.title: Where does רבי אלעאי learn the exemption for a non-Jewish partner?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי already uses צאנך for Jewish partners. So where does he learn that a partnership with a גוי is exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעאי, where does he learn the rule of a partnership with a non-Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי אלעאי's source for exempting a partnership with a גוי. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעאי, צאנך is already used up on Jewish partners. The גמרא assumes he also agrees that a partnership with a גוי is exempt, so he must have a separate source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? What is his source?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אִלְעַאי, שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹי מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ilai, partnership with a non-Jew, from where does he have it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אִלְעַאי, שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹי מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the רבנן back to רבי אלעאי and asks for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי אלעאי's source for exempting a flock shared with a גוי.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי learns it from 'the first of your grain'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי learns the exemption for a partnership with a גוי from the start of the same פסוק, 'ראשית דגנך,' which is about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the beginning of the verse: 'the first of your grain,' and not a partnership with a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעאי takes the rule from the first half of the פסוק, which talks about תרומה from grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says 'ראשית דגנך' (the first of your grain) and then 'ראשית גז צאנך.' 'Your grain' excludes produce shared with a גוי. רבי אלעאי applies that to the wool in the same פסוק as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, he learns it from
The beginning of the פסוק
'The first of your grain,' meaning תרומה

phrases.english: He derives it from the beginning of the verse,
'the first of your grain,'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: and not a partnership with a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'ראשית דגנך,' which excludes a partnership with a גוי and carries over to the wool in the same פסוק.

steps.title: Why the רבנן don't learn from 'your grain': the repeated 'first' splits the topics
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן cannot learn the wool law from 'ראשית דגנך,' because repeating the word ראשית before the wool shows a new topic has started.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? The repeated word 'first' cut off the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן need צאנך for a partnership with a גוי and do not use 'ראשית דגנך' like רבי אלעאי does. The next step gives רבי אלעאי's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'ראשית דגנך … וגז צאנך,' but it repeats the word ראשית before the wool. For the רבנן, that repeated word separates תרומה from ראשית הגז, so a rule from the grain half cannot be carried over to the wool. That is why they need צאנך itself to exempt a partnership with a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: It cut off the topic; it starts a new, separate subject

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעאי: צאנך exempts all partners, and 'ראשית דגנך' exempts a partnership with a גוי. רבנן: partners are obligated, and צאנך exempts only a partnership with a גוי, because the repeated ראשית keeps grain and wool separate.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: why don't the רבנן learn this from 'your grain' like רבי אלעאי?

phrases.english: 'The first' (of the shearing) broke off the topic.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the point is that the word ראשית is said a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the רבנן do not accept רבי אלעאי's source from step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the repeated word separates the two parts of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the רבנן could also learn the גוי exemption from 'ראשית דגנך' and leave צאנך free.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, the repeated ראשית separates the topics, so they need צאנך for a partnership with a גוי.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי: the 'and' joins the two topics back together
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי answers the רבנן: even though ראשית is repeated, the ו ('and') at the start of 'וראשית גז צאנך' connects the wool law back to 'ראשית דגנך,' so the two can be learned from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי אלעאי answer this? He says the letter ו ('and') goes back and joins the two topics together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעאי deals with the רבנן's argument from Step 39, and answers for him in a few words. He points to the small letter ו at the start of 'וראשית.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said a second ראשית means a new topic, so the wool cannot borrow from the תרומה part of the פסוק. רבי אלעאי agrees the word is repeated, but says the ו ('and') ties the wool right back to 'ראשית דגנך.' That is why he can still learn from 'דגנך' that a partnership with a גוי is exempt from ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו, which means 'and' at the start of a word
It goes back and combines it (joins the second topic to the first)
'And the first shearing of your sheep': the part of the פסוק about wool
'The first of your grain': the start of the פסוק, about תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree ראשית is repeated. The רבנן say that splits the topics apart, while רבי אלעאי says the ו ('and') joins them back together. That is how he can learn the exemption for a גוי partnership from 'דגנך.'
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעאי does not deny that ראשית is repeated. He just says the ו outweighs the repetition and keeps the two topics linked.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ilai, how does he answer?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how he answers the רבנן's point from the last step: that repeating ראשית starts a new topic.

phrases.english: The letter vav ('and') goes back and combines it.
phrases.notes: The ו is at the start of 'וראשית גז צאנך' in דברים 18:4. It ties the wool back to 'ראשית דגנך.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אלעאי's derivation (Step 38) against the רבנן's objection (Step 39) that the repeated ראשית separates the topics.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reading: the conjunction ו reconnects the separated clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating ראשית might make the wool clause a separate topic that cannot borrow from 'ראשית דגנך.'
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעאי, the ו in 'וראשית' joins the wool clause back to 'דגנך,' so the exemption for a partnership with a גוי can be learned from there.
